samples.summary: Vacuous assertion in the "passes supported methods straight through" test: `expect(typeof store.batch).toBe("function")` cannot fail even if `batch` were refused
samples.evidence: The test comment says this case is "what catches a proxy that over-refuses". But `asBoardStore`'s trap returns `() => { throw ... }` for a refused name (mem-board-store.ts:79-82), which is itself a function — so `typeof store.batch === "function"` holds identically whether `batch` is delegated or refused. The assertion is true regardless of the behaviour it claims to pin. `read()` and `canUndo()` in the same test ARE invoked and would throw, so only the `batch` line is fake; `batch` is also the mutation path the board readers/seed depend on, and it is exactly the one never called. A real check would be `store.batch(() => {})` (or asserting `store.batch !== store.addSlide`-style identity), i.e. actually exercising the pass-through.

samples.summary: `seedBoardElements()` ships with explicitly stated geometric invariants and no test at all — the slides equivalent was extracted into a module precisely so those invariants could be unit-tested
samples.evidence: The new seed's doc comment asserts three load-bearing properties: (a) every element sits inside the pinned 960x540 view at zoom 1, (b) no element's centre is covered by another (or `board.elementCenter` names one element and selects another — the exact manufactured-defect trap `slides-seed.test.ts:6-11` exists for), and (c) elements still overlap so a z-order change is visible. Nothing tests any of them: `seedBoardElements` is a non-exported function inside `page.tsx`, so it is not even reachable from vitest, whereas the slides seed lives in `slides-seed.ts` with `slides-seed.test.ts` covering exactly (a), (b), (c) plus a negative control. Reading the literals, (c) appears only partly true (only `note` 60..260/60..200 and `card` 220..460/150..310 overlap; `label` and `idea` overlap nothing), which is the kind of drift a test would have caught. The only executable check of the seed is in `packages/frontend/scripts/verify-hunt-oracles.mjs` READER_EXPECTATIONS, which asserts ids/order and `note.x===60 && note.w===200` only — and that script is invoked solely by `pnpm test:hunt-oracles` (packages/frontend/package.json:21) with no CI workflow referencing it.
searchedFor: packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/* (glob — only slides-seed.test.ts and mem-board-store.test.ts exist)

samples.summary: The new board charter's measured harness-specific claims (sticky controls unwired, `Insert image` "absent from the toolbar entirely", 7→12 control counts) are pinned by no test, unlike the sheet charter's equivalent claims
samples.evidence: `scripts/agent/hunt-ui.test.mjs:60-103` exists specifically because "a rubric stating a surface fact is a claim with an expiry date, and this is its test": it parses `formatting-toolbar.tsx`'s optional `on*?:` props and asserts the sheet rubric names every one, plus the spelled-out count. The board charter makes the same class of claims — `Sticky note`/`Sticky note color` do nothing because the harness omits `onInsertSticky`, `Insert image` is "absent from the toolbar entirely", and the toolbar "MORPHS" from exactly 7 to exactly 12 controls — with no analogous pin against `BoardToolbarProps`. The generic persona tests that now cover this charter (validate, rubric length, scope paths exist, "cannot see") assert nothing about these facts. The claim already looks stale: `board-toolbar.tsx:346-359` renders the `Insert image` toggle unconditionally and merely sets `disabled={... || !onInsertImage}`, so it is present-but-disabled, not absent — a wrong rubric fact is what produces false candidates, which is the failure the sheet test was written after.
searchedFor: glob for any board-toolbar test file

samples.summary: Several new board READER_EXPECTATIONS are type-only checks that hold whether or not the reader works
samples.evidence: `board.selection` only checks `Array.isArray(v)` (an always-empty or always-wrong selection passes — note the registry check clicks `board.elementCenter("card")` first, so asserting the clicked id is in the selection was available), `board.canUndo` only checks `typeof v === "boolean"` (a reader hardwired to `false` passes, and the charter/reader-table both claim undo is real here), and `board.pointAt`/`elementCenter`/`handleCenter` only check finiteness rather than the value implied by the pinned `{panX:0,panY:0,zoom:1}` viewport where world px == screen px (e.g. `board.pointAt(100,100)` and `card`'s centre are exactly predictable from the seed). `checkBoardViewport` does real work, so the core off-screen/world-coord behaviour is exercised — but only inside a script no CI lane invokes (`pnpm test:hunt-oracles`, packages/frontend/package.json:21; no workflow references it).

verdict.reason: Verified directly. mem-board-store.ts:79-82 returns `() => { throw ... }` for a refused name, and mem-board-store.ts:87 returns `value.bind(target)` for a supported one — both are functions, so `expect(typeof store.batch).toBe("function")` (mem-board-store.test.ts:55) passes identically whether `batch` is delegated or refused. The test's own comment (lines 51-52) claims this case "catches a proxy that over-refuses" and names the batch path, so the assertion is presented as coverage for a behavior it cannot detect; it only distinguishes present-vs-absent. The neighbouring assertions (line 54 `store.read().slides`, line 56 `store.canUndo()`) are genuinely invoked, confirming the defect is isolated to line 55 exactly as claimed. No compensating coverage exists: `asBoardStore` is only constructed at test lines 45, 53, 70 and production page.tsx:496, and `batch` is invoked only on the UNWRAPPED store at page.tsx:298 (seedSlides) and visual/slides-scenarios.tsx:881 — never through the proxy in a test. Code is present as described, unguarded, and vacuous assertions are squarely in the test-adequacy lane, so no refutation ground applies.

verdict.reason: Verified directly. `seedBoardElements()` (page.tsx:250-294) states three invariants in its doc comment (page.tsx:238-249): every element inside the pinned 960x540 view at zoom 1, no element's centre covered by another, and residual overlap so z-order changes are visible. None are tested. The hunt directory contains only slides-seed.test.ts and mem-board-store.test.ts; slides-seed.ts:26-31 SEED_FRAMES holds only the slides frames (card/badge/title/body), so slides-seed.test.ts's centre/overlap/in-canvas loops never see the board rects, and mem-board-store.test.ts covers proxy refusal semantics only. I searched wide for a counterexample: repo-wide grep for the seeded id set (only page.tsx:293 and verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:298,302), every *.test.* file mentioning harness/board, scripts/agent/hunt-*.test.mjs, scripts/test/*, and all elementCenter uses under packages/frontend/scripts. The slides analogue of the covered-centre check exists as checkSlidesTargeting (verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:535-561) but has no board counterpart: enumerating the driver (lines 1719-1787), the only board check is checkBoardViewport (825-875), which covers off-screen refusal, panning, and world-coordinate stability — not centre coverage or overlap. Board seed assertions are limited to READER_EXPECTATIONS 299-317 (id order, label text, note.x/w, count 4, pinned viewport); invariant (a) is only incidentally exercised for `card` via the finite-point expectation at line 320 plus the off-screen refusal at bridge.ts:589, i.e. one of four elements. That lane is also not in CI: test:hunt-oracles (packages/frontend/package.json:21) -> verify:hunt:oracles (package.json:16), with no reference anywhere under .github/ or in verify:ci/verify:self aggregators. A new behavior with explicitly stated geometric invariants and no meaningful test covering them is the 'missing tests' branch of this lens.

verdict.reason: I could find no test pinning the board charter's harness-specific claims. Greps across scripts/** for board-author, Sticky, MORPHS, onInsert*, BoardToolbarProps and *toolbar.tsx show the only charter-fact pin is the sheet one (hunt-ui.test.mjs:60-103, reading formatting-toolbar.tsx); the surface-constraints test (hunt-ui.test.mjs:105-139) asserts sheet/doc facts only, and no scripts/agent test file references the board at all. Board-side tests I followed cover other things: board-toolbar-state.test.ts only exercises getToolbarState/canUngroupSelection over a board store (no control inventory, no props), and the browser lane verify-hunt-oracles.mjs pins board READERS (elementCount 4 at :313, viewport/pointAt at :316-324, scroll independence at :825) while its toolbar checks are sheet-scoped (:943) and its control-inventory check is doc-scoped on Bold (:1110). So the 7->12 control counts, the sticky-controls-are-inert claim and the Insert image claim are unpinned, while the harness mount that makes them true (harness/hunt/page.tsx:743-756, omitting onInsertSticky/onInsertImage) and the props that would break them (board-toolbar.tsx:79-81) are one edit away from silent drift. One nuance that reduces the reviewer's "already stale" framing but not the gap: Insert image IS rendered unconditionally and merely disabled (board-toolbar.tsx:346-359), but domControls skips disabled elements (hunt-ui-dom.mjs:43), so the charter's "absent" is true of what the agent can see.
